svg.title: ARMA vs ARIMA
svg.desc: ARMA models an already stationary series; ARIMA differences first, models, then integrates back to levels.
svg.text: ARMA vs ARIMA — what differencing changes
Modeling a series that is already stationary, or differencing it first
interval width settles at a constant
then integrate back to the level
Starts from the last observed level
an MA unit root appears and
Set d with a unit root test
Choose p and q directly, no differencing
Level y — a trend is present
First difference Δy — back around a mean
Choosing d is the first step
Starts from the last observed level
Shocks stay in the level, so forecasts never come back
ARIMA is ARMA plus differencing, and that one addition changes the nature of the forecast.
Converging to the mean or starting from the last level — that is what splits long-horizon forecasts.
Decide with a unit root test; the urge to difference once more is what causes over-differencing.
